note: Thomason-Sassi et al. (2011) found latency to problem behavior was inversely related to response rate, supporting latency as a viable FA measure that reduces exposure to problem behavior. D states the opposite relation; B and C contradict the paper's central finding that latency corresponded with rate-based outcomes across conditions.

Rapidly alternating two conditions within a single participant and comparing the resulting data paths is the defining use case for an alternating treatments design. A requires multiple independent baselines and is slow, B compares treatment to baseline rather than two treatments and requires reversibility, and D shapes one behavior toward a terminal goal rather than comparing procedures.
